profile.oneLineIdentity: A positional zone-engineering tree: it plants two kinds of persistent 5 ft tokens — ally-buff squares and single-use keen-damage/Restrain traps — then spends every remaining talent upgrading, relocating, linking, remotely triggering and mass-detonating them, handing most of its actual output to allies as free actions. Comparatively it is the least distinctive of the placed-token deity trees: its ally-facing half is a near-clone of deity/Civilization's Foundation half (and shares deity/Order's Covenant clauses a third time), its trap half is a slower, ally-dependent version of deity/Destruction's Charge half, and its one clean corpus ownership is Snare's untested Restrained.

axes.evidence: THREE talents carry a roll formula and all three ride the Snare hazard; a fourth (Hexmark) adds a flat rider that fires off ANY damage source. Snare (depth 0, L1): (@tier)d(2 * @skills.green.rank + 2) + @attr.awa type=keen — 1d6+AWA at Tier 1 rank 2, 2d8+AWA at Tier 2 rank 3. Inevitable Snare (depth 1, L2): additional (@tier)d(...) keen. Foreknown Strike (depth 2, L3): additional (@tier)d(...) — its PROSE omits the damage type but the authored formula is type=keen. Hexmark (depth 1, L2): flat +[Tier] keen per damage instance, no formula. Thread of Inevitability (depth 3, L4) deals damage by detonating every unsprung Snare at once. Real and repeatable, but only ONE talent creates damage (census: 1 source / 3 amplify), every point is a rider on a trap firing, it is all keen (Deflect-reduced — no vital, no spirit anywhere), and there is no talent that simply attacks a target you choose. COMPARATIVE CHECK: 3 is the right band, not 4 — deity/Destruction carries SIX damage formulas including energy AoE that ignores deflect (Pinpoint Charge, The Unmooring), and deity/Knowledge deals Deflect-ignoring Vital; both are structurally parallel trap/mark trees and both out-damage Fate on the same actions.

Snare / Inevitable Snare / Foreknown Strike all scale on BOTH axes — (@tier) dice of size (2*@skills.green.rank+2), so L1-5 rank 2 = 1d6 and L6+ rank 3 = 2d8, a clean doubling-plus-die-upgrade at L6. Repeatable every round rather than once-per-rest. Two brakes: the tree can sustain only [Tier] unsprung Snares (ONE at levels 1-5, so one detonation per round is the ceiling), and it generates zero Investiture, so the Inevitable Snare upgrade is not affordable every round until Tier 2. Hexmark's flat [Tier] rider does not meaningfully scale. Note the same (@tier)d(2*rank+2) shape is used by Destruction, Civilization and Knowledge — the scaling curve is the deity-atlas house formula, not a Fate strength.

CORRECTED DOWN from 4 on comparative grounds. The quality of Snare's Restrained is real: depth 0, L1, 1 Action + 1 Investiture, movement 0 plus disadvantage on everything but escape, for a full round, with NO test required — genuinely the best single condition application in the corpus per instance, and Fate owns the only untested Restrain (leyline/Green's Grasping Vines, the only other Restrained source, needs a Green test AND 1 Investiture per turn to maintain). But 4 means 'one of the better options in the game for this', and the delivery cannot carry that: only TWO condition-applying talents in 9, the [Tier] sustain cap allows exactly ONE Restrain per round through levels 1-5, and until Foreknown Strike (depth 2, L3) the enemy must voluntarily step into a 5 ft square you nominated — an enemy that stands still, flies, or shoots from cover eats zero control. Measured across the corpus by condition/denial talents per tree: leyline/Green 10, leyline/Black 8, deity/Death 4, leyline/Red 4, deity/Power 3 (Kneel's Compelled, Absolute Authority, Unstoppable Advance's Immobilized), deity/Order 3, deity/Civilization 3 — and leyline/Blue's Absolute Stillness applies 0 Speed AND no Reactions. Fate sits at 2 talents. That is a 3.

Hexmark — the Hexmarked target takes an additional [Tier] keen whenever it takes damage from ANY source while within 10 ft of your Ordained Ground or unsprung Snares; a genuine vulnerability mark, but +1 damage at Tier 1 and doubly conditional. Bulwark Ground — attacks against an ally on your square cannot benefit from advantage. CORRECTED: this is NOT corpus-unique. leyline/Green **Natural Order** ('enemies within your Attunement Range cannot benefit from illusions, magical concealment, or advantage gained from deception') is a second advantage-denial clause, scene-long and against every enemy in range. And in a tri-state advantage system (SYSTEM-PRIMER: None/Advantage/Disadvantage, net state not a count) IMPOSING disadvantage is a strict superset of denying advantage — leyline/White **Voice of Authority** ('When an enemy within Attunement Range targets an ally with a hostile action, spend 1 Investiture to impose disadvantage'), heroic/Leader **Valiant Intervention**, and heroic/Warrior **Defensive Position** (two disadvantages) all do it. Score held at 2.

Two talents, and the numbers are one ally's worth. Ordained Ground — an ally that begins its turn on the square gains +1 to ALL defenses; the sustain cap is [Tier] squares, so at levels 1-5 that is exactly ONE 5 ft square. Bulwark Ground — temporary HP equal to your tier, ONE temp HP per round through Tier 1, plus the advantage denial. Entirely ally-facing and positional: the Fate character personally gains no defence, no reaction-based mitigation, no interception, no resistance. COMPARATIVE: deity/Civilization delivers strictly more of the identical effect — Lay Foundation is a 10 ft square (four times the area) with the same Free Action, same 1 Investiture, same +1 to all defenses, same 'sustain up to your tier', plus Bonds of Community (temp HP equal to your White to every ally in any Foundation) and Magnum Opus (+2 to all defenses); deity/Order's Covenant grants the same +1 to two characters with no square at all.

Checked all nine talents and all nine wiring blocks: zero heal formulas (dossier header: 3 damage, 0 heal; every authored damage block is null or type=keen), and no text restores Health, Focus or Investiture. Bulwark Ground grants temporary HP, which is not healing. Notable given the tree gates on White, whose Draw Mana rider IS the party heal — but that comes from the attunement key, not from this tree.

Judged as 'what a character actually gains in one round', per the binary-advantage rule. The tree grants ZERO advantage and zero rerolls — the advantage-ledger's only Fate entry is Bulwark Ground, and it DENIES advantage. The buff content is Ordained Ground's +1 to all defenses (dual-coded with protection, not double-weighted) plus three talents routing the standard Aid action. Aid is a 1-focus Reaction every character already has, so the roll-bonus content is 'one Aid on one ally per round, cheaper or further'. COMPARATIVE: deity/Order's Covenant already grants Aid at full Attunement Range from an ENTRY node, and Concord already makes an ally's Aid a Free Action AND adds Presence damage — Fate's Aid routing is the weaker reissue of an existing deity design.

CORRECTED DOWN from 4. Four talents touch the axis, tying Fate for the corpus lead by COUNT — but the calibration rule says granting an action a character already had is worth much less than granting a NEW one, and only ONE of Fate's four qualifies. Foreknown Strike grants a genuinely NEW Free Action (trigger an unsprung Snare within 30 ft). The other three route STANDARD actions: Weave the Thread converts Aid to a Free Action (deity/Order's Concord already does this plus damage); Thread of Inevitability grants a free Strike or Aid, capped by the tree's own [Tier] limit to ONE ally at levels 1-5; Read the Threads' 'Free Action' moves a MARKER, not a character. Against the corpus this cannot be a 4: heroic/Envoy **Foresight** is a Passive granting an additional Reaction EVERY turn; heroic/Leader **Synchronized Assault** gives allies up to your Leadership ranks a whole ACTION; heroic/Scholar **Turning Point** gives you and your allies an Action; heroic/Warrior's Flamestance and Windstance gain an Action; deity/Knowledge **The Final Study** gives EVERY ally a free Strike with no tier cap. Also re-verified: granting an ally a Free Action is not near-unique (Order Concord, Civilization Trade Routes and Siege Form, Knowledge Hunter's Discipline and Death Mark, Destruction Set Charge), and Weave the Thread's 'free Reactive Strike' is not established to bypass the 1-Reaction cap.

Looked for movement, teleport or repositioning of characters: nothing. Read the Threads moves an Ordained Ground square or unsprung Snare up to 10 ft — that repositions a placed token (authored handler edha-marker-command mode=move, maxFt 10, operating on markers), not a creature. The tree ANTI-synergises with mobility: its ally-facing half requires allies to stand still on 5 ft squares. Contrast the structurally identical deity/Civilization Trade Routes, which DOES teleport an ally between the two linked squares as a Free Action once per turn — Fate's link talent pointedly does not, and costs 2 Investiture where Trade Routes costs 1.

The defining pillar, held at 5 on saturation — but the exclusivity claims underneath it were wrong. All nine talents place, upgrade, move, link, trigger or key off a placed token. CORRECTED (a): Fate is NOT the only 100%-zone tree — **deity/Destruction is also 9 of 9** (Pyre and Set Charge place; Combustion Chain spreads dangerous terrain on a kill; Walking Ruin makes every space you move through dangerous terrain; Concussive Yield and Pinpoint Charge ride the placed Charge; Fault Line lays a 60 ft line of dangerous terrain; Cascading Failure merges zones; The Unmooring merges every zone in the scene), and Destruction's zones are strictly more active — they damage on their own, spread each turn, and merge — where every Fate token is inert until a creature interacts with it. CORRECTED (b): 'at least SIX talents place or designate a specific square' is a large undercount; the real figure is roughly TWENTY across six trees (Destruction 8, leyline/Green 4+, Fate 3, Civilization 2 incl. Bastion, Death's Bone Garden, heroic/Hunter's Deadly Trap). Fate's distinction is saturation of REFERENCE, not of placement, and it shares even that with Destruction.

Read the Threads (depth 1, L2, 1 Action + 1 Inv) — complete declared foreknowledge of one character's turn, repeatable every round. Strong in isolation but the ONLY information talent in the tree. CORPUS CHECK, and Fate loses the comparison it was implicitly winning: deity/Order **Lawkeeper's Eye** is a **Passive** that delivers the same fact ('you learn the bound character's intended action on its next turn') as a free rider on placing an Edict, AND adds advantage on attack tests against that character for you and your allies — same information, no Action, no Investiture; leyline/Blue **Read Intent** costs 1 Investiture and a Blue test; leyline/Blue **Forewarned** is a depth-0 Passive predicting an action type every round for free. Fate pays the most and is the only one of the four paying a full Action. Held at 2 — not 1 (a whole talent, not a rider), not 3 (one talent, out-priced by three others).

Read all nine texts: no persuasion, command, deception, intimidation, reputation, Compelled, or any out-of-combat leverage over people. Even Read the Threads reads intent without allowing you to alter it.

Everything is scene-scoped and combat-framed. Two incidental non-combat uses: Read the Threads works on any character in range, and a Snare is a literal trap that could be laid on a doorway. No travel, crafting, survival, downtime or environmental problem-solving. COMPARATIVE: heroic/Hunter's Deadly Trap is a CONCEALED trap laid at depth 0 with no Investiture cost, which is the out-of-scene trap use Fate's Snare only gestures at.

Ordained Ground squares and Snares are inert placed tokens with no statblock, no actions and no independent existence — the free Strikes in Weave the Thread and Thread of Inevitability are taken by real allies. (Contrast deity/Civilization, whose second token economy IS a statted Combat Construct with HP, deflect, Speed, defenses and an attack that acts on your initiative.)

Zero generation, confirmed against every Cost field. No talent returns Investiture, Focus or Opportunity, and the tree never touches Opportunity or the Plot Die. SEVEN of nine talents spend Investiture (11 to deploy the full kit once). Matches the census line 'Fate 0 regen / 7 costers'. DEFLATION CHECK RUN AND PASSED — I looked specifically for economy hiding in riders and found none: the nearest thing is Weave the Thread converting an ally's Aid Reaction into a Free Action (action economy, not resource generation; Aid's 1 focus is not waived). By contrast deity/Sovereignty's Expose returns 1 Investiture on a failed test, and Chaos, Death, Life, Knowledge and Sovereignty each carry one regen talent. Fate is one of five deity trees at 0 regen and the only tree in the atlas whose nine talents never mention Opportunity, Focus or the Plot Die at all.

damageTalents.name: Snare
damageTalents.dice: (@tier)d(2 * @skills.green.rank + 2) + @attr.awa keen — 1d6+AWA at Tier 1 rank 2; 2d8+AWA at Tier 2 rank 3
damageTalents.action: 1 Action to place (+1 Investiture); damage resolves later on trigger
damageTalents.note: THE tree's only damage SOURCE. CONDITIONAL/DELAYED: damage only happens when the first enemy ENTERS the square. Until Foreknown Strike (depth 2) the enemy must cooperate. Also applies Restrained until the start of your next turn, with no test. Consumed on trigger; only [Tier] unsprung Snares may be sustained (ONE at levels 1-5), and the authored handler evicts the oldest at cap. COMPARATIVE: deity/Destruction's Set Charge is the same entry-node shape at the same price (1 Action, 1 Investiture, cap tier, scene duration) but adds 'You may detonate any of your Charges as a Free Action on your turn' — the capability Fate does not reach until depth 2, and then only through an ally.

damageTalents.name: Inevitable Snare
damageTalents.dice: additional (@tier)d(2 * @skills.green.rank + 2) keen — +1d6 at Tier 1; +2d8 at Tier 2
damageTalents.action: Free Action rider at placement (+1 Investiture on top of Snare's 1)
damageTalents.note: RIDER on a rider: only pays out if the upgraded Snare triggers. Also forces the triggering target to test Speed vs. your Green (riderSkill 'spd', riderColor 'green', riderFailStatus 'disoriented'); on a failure, Disoriented until end of its next turn. Doubles the Snare's Investiture price, which is what makes it unsustainable at Tier 1. Its exact structural twin is deity/Destruction's Pinpoint Charge — same depth 1, same Free Action, same additional 1 Investiture — which adds Intellect to its dice AND ignores the target's deflect, where Inevitable Snare's dice stay Deflect-reducible keen.

damageTalents.name: Hexmark
damageTalents.dice: flat [Tier] keen (1 at Tier 1, 2 at Tier 2) — no roll formula
damageTalents.note: TRIPLY CONDITIONAL RIDER, and NOT delivered by the Snare hazard: the Snare trigger only APPLIES the mark; damage then fires whenever the marked enemy takes damage from ANY source while within 10 ft of one of your Ordained Ground squares or unsprung Snares. Fires off ALLIES' damage too — but at +1 keen per instance for the whole of levels 1-5. Costs your one Reaction. COMPARATIVE: deity/Knowledge's Insight mark does the same job with Deflect-ignoring Vital damage and it stacks.

damageTalents.name: Foreknown Strike
damageTalents.dice: additional (@tier)d(2 * @skills.green.rank + 2), authored type=keen — +1d6 at Tier 1; +2d8 at Tier 2
damageTalents.action: 2 Actions + 2 Investiture, once, lasts the scene
damageTalents.note: RIDER, but the load-bearing one: it converts the Snare from 'hope the enemy walks in' into a party-detonated bomb. COMPARATIVE COST FINDING (new this pass): deity/Destruction gets self-detonation as one clause of its depth-0 ENTRY with no ally required; Fate pays a depth-2 talent, 2 Actions and 2 Investiture for a worse version that outsources the trigger to another player's positioning and Free Action. TEXT/DATA DIVERGENCE: the card says 'an additional [Tier][Die] damage' with NO damage type; the authored damage block supplies type='keen'. WORDING FLAG: 'treating the center of the Snare's space as the triggering character' names a square, not a creature — who takes the damage when no enemy occupies the square is undefined.

damageTalents.name: Thread of Inevitability
damageTalents.dice: no damage expression of its own; detonates EVERY unsprung Snare at full value and grants a free Strike or Aid from the ally on every active Ordained Ground square
damageTalents.action: 3 Actions + 3 Investiture, once per scene, delayed until a declared event occurs
damageTalents.note: HAZARD-DELIVERED damage. Payload is capped by the tree's OWN sustain limits ([Tier] Snares + [Tier] squares), so at Tier 1 the 'detonate everything' capstone detonates exactly one Snare and grants exactly one free Strike. Trigger reliability is partly GM-adjudicated. Same undefined-target wording as Foreknown Strike, plus a second flaw: 'a free Strike or Aid against the nearest enemy' — Aid targets an ally, not an enemy.

damageAccounting.peakDamagePerAction: ~3 [Tier][Die] + Awareness of keen damage per Snare detonated, but only on the ally-triggered path. At Tier 1 with all three online (legal by L3): 1d6 (Snare) + 1d6 (Inevitable) + 1d6 (Foreknown — the card scopes that die to a Snare 'triggered this way', i.e. ally-detonated; an enemy who simply walks in eats 2d6+AWA, not 3d6+AWA) + AWA = 3d6 + AWA, ~10.5 + AWA. At Tier 2 rank 3 (L6+) the same three packages are 6d8 + AWA, ~27 + AWA, plus Restrained and a Speed-vs-Green Disoriented, for ONE of the placer's Actions plus 2 Investiture and one ally Free Action. Hexmark contributes only a flat [Tier]. COMPARATIVE CEILING: deity/Destruction's Cascading Failure detonates ANY NUMBER of Charges at 10 ft radius each with a bonus die for overlap, and The Unmooring does it at 15 ft radius ignoring deflect — Fate's 'peak' is one square, one enemy, Deflect-reducible.
damageAccounting.repeatability: Once per round, hard-capped by the sustain limit of [Tier] unsprung Snares (ONE at levels 1-5, TWO at 6-10) and by Investiture: a full-value Inevitable Snare costs 2 Investiture, needing two Draw Mana Actions at Tier 1 and therefore NOT sustainable; at Tier 2 Draw Mana returns 2 per Action so 'Draw Mana + place Inevitable Snare' is sustainable indefinitely with an Action to spare. At Tier 1 you cannot hold a second Snare until the first has sprung (the authored handler evicts the oldest). The capstone burst is once per scene.
damageAccounting.verdict: REAL but wholly conditional and entirely keen. Five talents participate in damage; ONE (Snare) actually creates it and three are riders, with Hexmark riding any damage source. The tree can deal damage from depth 0 / level 1, which is early, but until Foreknown Strike at depth 2 / level 3 the enemy decides whether any of it lands — a gate the structurally parallel deity/Destruction does not have, because Set Charge includes self-detonation at depth 0. Damage scales cleanly on both tier and Green rank and repeats every round, yet it is entirely Deflect-reducible keen (no vital, no spirit, nothing ignoring deflect — every comparable deity tree has at least one) and the tree cannot aim a single point of damage at a target of its choosing without first getting a token under that target's feet. Cleanly, ZERO damage false-positives: no mitigation talent even uses the word 'damage'. Checked in the other direction too — no summon, no Afflicted tick, no redirect, and no zone that damages on its own (contrast Civilization's Bastion, Death's Bone Garden, Destruction's dangerous terrain).

powerByDepth.note: Lopsided. Snare is a strong entry — 1 Action + 1 Investiture for [Tier][Die]+AWA and a full round of untested Restrained, repeatable from level 1, and it carries the tree's one clean corpus ownership. Ordained Ground DOES deliver the half of the stated fantasy it was written for, but it is the corpus's THIRD issue of one design: deity/Civilization's Lay Foundation is the same Free Action, same 1 Investiture, same '+1 to all defenses for allies beginning their turn there', same 'sustain up to your tier' — on a 10 ft square instead of 5 ft — and deity/Order's Covenant carries the same clauses again (+1 to all defenses, Aid at extended range, sustain up to your tier) with no square to stand on. Neither Fate entry delivers the foreknowledge half of the archetype, which lives only in Read the Threads at depth 1.

powerByDepth.exemplars: Foreknown Strike; Weave the Thread; Read the Threads; Inevitable Snare
powerByDepth.note: CHECKED AND UPHELD at 4, with the comparative caveat recorded rather than folded into the number. Foreknown Strike is the pivot; Weave the Thread converts an ally's Aid into a Free Action and adds a Reactive Strike; Read the Threads is complete foreknowledge plus a free reposition; Inevitable Snare roughly doubles trap output and adds Disoriented. Bulwark Ground's temp-HP half and Hexmark are the band's dead weight. Depths verified: Read the Threads and Inevitable Snare are depth 1 / L2; Foreknown Strike and Weave the Thread are depth 2 / L3. CAVEAT: each of the four is out-priced by an equivalent elsewhere — Foreknown Strike buys at depth 2 / L3 / 2 Actions / 2 Inv what Destruction's Set Charge includes at depth 0; Weave the Thread is Order's Concord minus the Presence damage, and Civilization's Trade Routes links the same two squares for 1 Investiture and teleports; Read the Threads is Order's Lawkeeper's Eye as a paid Action instead of a free Passive rider. The band is the tree's best relative to itself, not to the atlas.

Under-delivers for a capstone. 3 Actions (an entire Slow turn; impossible on a Fast turn's 2 Actions) plus 3 Investiture plus once-per-scene, and the payload is throttled by the tree's own [Tier] sustain caps — one Snare and one free Strike at levels 1-5. It does exactly what the deity guide asks a snare-tree capstone to do, and can then only reach one snare. Two other deity capstones at the identical price detonate materially more: Destruction's The Unmooring (all Charges, radius up to 15 ft, ignoring deflect, [Tier][Die] + Intellect each, plus every dangerous-terrain zone merged and upgraded) and Knowledge's The Final Study ([Tier][Die] Vital per Insight stack plus a free Strike for EVERY ally in Attunement Range, uncapped).

profile.frontOrBackLoaded: MIDDLE-loaded. The entries are cheap and one of them is genuinely good, the depth 1-2 band carries the tree and contains all four of its best talents, and the capstone is the weakest talent per unit of cost because the tree's own sustain caps limit what it can detonate. Unusually for a deity tree the whole thing is reachable by level 4 (depth 3 capstone = 4 talents owned) and nothing gates above rank 2, so there is no level-6 discontinuity in ACCESS — only in output, where the Tier 1 to Tier 2 step doubles both the number of dice and the number of sustainable tokens at once.
uniqueOwnership: The only UNTESTED Restrain in the corpus, and the tree's one unambiguous ownership. Restrained appears on exactly two of 365 talents (leyline/Green Grasping Vines and Fate's Snare); Grasping Vines needs a Green test AND 1 Investiture per turn to maintain, where Snare applies it automatically to the first enemy that enters, from a depth-0 entry, repeatably. The nearest trap analogue, heroic/Hunter's Deadly Trap (also depth 0, L1, also a 5 ft trap square), applies the weaker Immobilized — movement 0 only, no disadvantage — and requires a Survival test.

The only talent that hands an ALLY the trigger for the caster's own hazard (Foreknown Strike). Verified against every 'as a Free Action' and detonation clause in the corpus: deity/Destruction's Set Charge lets the PLACER detonate, deity/Civilization's Bastion triggers on enemy entry, and nothing else delegates a hazard trigger to an ally. NOTE THE PRICE — this is ownership of a WORSE version of a capability: Destruction gets self-detonation as one clause of a depth-0 entry, Fate pays a depth-2 talent, 2 Actions and 2 Investiture and still needs an ally standing on a square.

The only DELAYED TRIGGER declared as an arbitrary narrative event: Thread of Inevitability lets the player name 'a character drops to 0 HP', 'an ally reaches a designated location' or 'the GM raises the stakes'. Two comparators bound the claim rather than break it — deity/Destruction's Set Charge declares its own trigger at placement but from a mechanical menu ('when target moves', 'when target takes damage', 'when a character enters this square'), and leyline/Blue's Forewarned declares a character and an action type at the start of EVERY round as a free depth-0 Passive. Fate's is unique only in being unbounded by a mechanical event type, and is by far the most expensive of the three.

The only tree that converts foreknowledge into physical board state in one activation — Read the Threads reads a target's declared next action and movement and then, as a Free Action, slides a trap into the path it just told you about. leyline/Blue Read Intent and deity/Order Lawkeeper's Eye read the same intent (Lawkeeper's Eye for free, as a Passive, and it adds advantage on attacks against the target); leyline/Blue Intercept converts a foreseen action into disadvantage. None of them moves a hazard with the answer.

DOWNGRADED, NOT UNIQUE — 'the only source of advantage DENIAL in the game' (Bulwark Ground) is FALSE. leyline/Green **Natural Order** also denies advantage ('enemies within your Attunement Range cannot benefit from illusions, magical concealment, or advantage gained from deception', scene-long, every enemy in range). And because the system implements advantage as a tri-state where net state decides, imposing disadvantage is a strict superset of denying it — leyline/White **Voice of Authority** protects an ally against ANY hostile action at Attunement Range for 1 Investiture with no square required, heroic/Leader **Valiant Intervention** imposes disadvantage on tests against your allies, and heroic/Warrior **Defensive Position** stacks two. Bulwark Ground owns the PHRASING, not the effect, and its version is the most positionally constrained of the five.

DOWNGRADED, NOT UNIQUE — 'the most zone-saturated tree in the corpus / no other tree is 100% zone' is FALSE. **deity/Destruction is also 9 of 9**, and its zones spread, merge and damage on their own where Fate's are inert until a creature interacts with them. Fate ties for saturation and loses on zone quality. The related count 'at least six talents place a specific square' is also an undercount: roughly twenty do, across six trees.

WITHDRAWN, SELF-CONTRADICTED — 'the only tree that keeps its two token economies strictly separate' is refuted by the tree's own text. Hexmark's damage rider fires within 10 ft of 'any of your Ordained Ground squares OR unsprung Snares'; Foreknown Strike requires an ally on an Ordained Ground square to trigger a Snare; Thread of Inevitability fires both at once. The two economies are explicitly cross-linked from depth 1 onward. (Running two placed-token economies is not unique either: deity/Civilization runs Foundations plus a statted Combat Construct, deity/Destruction runs Charges plus dangerous terrain.)

WITHDRAWN — 'the only talent whose granted Reactive Strike is worded free' (Weave the Thread). leyline/Green **Drive the Prey** and deity/Sovereignty **Expose** both grant allies Reactive Strikes. And 'free' is not established to mean 'does not consume the Reaction'; the likelier reading is that it waives Reactive Strike's 1-focus cost.
gaps: No healing whatsoever — nothing restores Health, Focus or Investiture to anyone.

No resource generation of any kind, and no interaction with Opportunity or the Plot Die at all, despite gating on White (whose design identity is explicitly Plot Die and Opportunity coordination). Seven of nine talents spend Investiture and the tree gives none back — one of five deity trees at 0 regen, and the only tree in the atlas whose nine talents never mention Opportunity, Focus or the Plot Die at all.

No self-mobility, no teleport, no repositioning of characters. Worse than neutral: the ally-facing half actively requires allies to stand still on 5 ft squares. Its own structural twin, deity/Civilization's Trade Routes, teleports the ally between the linked squares for 1 Investiture; Weave the Thread does not, and costs 2.

NO SELF-TRIGGER UNTIL DEPTH 2 — the sharpest comparative gap, new this pass. The placer can never spring their own trap. deity/Destruction's Set Charge includes 'you may detonate any of your Charges as a Free Action on your turn' in its depth-0 ENTRY; Fate must reach Foreknown Strike (depth 2, L3, 2 Actions + 2 Investiture) and then still needs an ally standing on an Ordained Ground square who will spend a Free Action. Against a stationary boss, a flyer, or a ranged enemy behind cover, the entire Snare half of the tree is inert for the first two levels of the tree and conditional thereafter.
No way to deal a single point of damage to a target of your choosing. Every point is delivered by a token a creature must first stand on or beside.

No Deflect-ignoring damage. All four damage clauses are keen. Every comparable deity tree has at least one: Destruction (Pinpoint Charge and The Unmooring ignore deflect), Knowledge (Vital), Death (Vital), Power (spirit).

Nothing works in an ambush or a scene you did not get to set up. Every talent is a scene-length placement made during the scene at Action cost, and the caps are [Tier] tokens. heroic/Hunter, whose intent file makes the same preparation promise, at least gets a CONCEALED trap at depth 0.
No personal defence. Every protective effect is ally-facing and requires the ally to be on your square.
No social influence, no interrogation, no reputation, no command.
No exploration, travel, downtime, crafting or survival content.
No condition removal and no counter to enemy control — the tree applies Restrained and Disoriented but cannot lift either from an ally.

No zone that acts on its own. Every token is inert until a creature interacts with it; there is no per-turn hazard tick (contrast Death's Bone Garden, Destruction's dangerous terrain, Civilization's Bastion). It also creates no difficult terrain, despite the Green gate — the only placed-token tree in the corpus that does not.

claims.claim: PATH DESCRIPTION: 'the oracle who sets the board before initiative is rolled... Her blessed do not react to the battle; they have already read it.'
claims.evidence: No talent operates before initiative or outside a scene. Every token is placed during the scene at Action and Investiture cost, all durations are 'for the scene', and the sustain caps are [Tier] — ONE square and ONE Snare at levels 1-5. The board is not set before initiative; it is assembled one token per round during the fight. And the tree does react: Hexmark is a Reaction, and seven of nine talents wait on someone else acting.

claims.claim: CROSS-TREE (added by this pass, and the finding lens A cannot see): the promise Fate's intent file makes is ALSO made, in nearly the same words, by TWO other trees' intent files — and each delivers its half earlier and cheaper.
claims.evidence: heroic/Hunter's intent: 'you don't have to be more powerful than your quarry, so long as you're better prepared... Through careful planning, Hunters choose when and where to strike, securing an upper hand through clever use of traps, high ground, and the element of surprise... Archers shape the battlefield before the frontline confrontation... methodical preparation culminating in an exhilarating onslaught.' Hunter delivers that at depth 0 with **Deadly Trap** — a CONCEALED 5 ft trap, no Investiture, damage plus Immobilized plus difficult terrain, or an Afflicted variant. leyline/Blue's intent: 'Blue leyline mages read the battle a beat before it happens... A Blue mage prefers to know, to prepare, and to redirect: intercepting an attack foreseen.' claims.claim: PATH DESCRIPTION: 'lays Snares on the squares an enemy has not yet chosen to enter. When the foreseen step comes, the trap is already waiting.'

Lay Foundation (deity/Civilization) vs Ordained Ground: both Free Action, both 1 Investiture, both 'designate a [size] square in Attunement Range... for the scene', both give allies that begin their turn there '+1 to all defenses until the start of their next turn', both 'sustain up to your tier' — Civilization's square is 10 ft to Fate's 5 ft. **Covenant (deity/Order)** carries the clauses a third time: '+1 to all defenses when within Attunement Range of each other, and may use the Aid action targeting each other at any range within Attunement Range... You may sustain up to your tier active Covenants' — Ordained Ground's defense bonus AND its Aid-range extension, at better range, with no square to stand on. For the scene, they are linked: an ally standing [in / on] either linked [Foundation / square] may [teleport to the other / use the Aid action] as a Free Action once per [turn / round]' — and Trade Routes costs 1 Investiture to Weave the Thread's 2. intentDrift.actuallyIs: Empirically this is a battlefield-engineering tree, not an oracle. Eight of its nine talents place, upgrade, move, link, remotely detonate and mass-detonate persistent 5 ft tokens; exactly one talent (Read the Threads) does foreknowledge, and it is a depth-1 optional pick that acts after placement rather than before it. Its real competitive strengths are zone saturation (9 of 9 talents, tied with deity/Destruction), a repeatable UNTESTED Restrained that no other talent in the corpus offers, and handing free actions to allies who hold ground — a support-engineer who builds an ally-anchored kill box. THE 'SOMETHING' TEST, answered honestly: Fate's something is 'ally-buff squares and enemy traps in one linked economy' — and each half is done better by an existing tree. deity/Civilization's Foundations are four times the area with the same bonus, and Bastion turns those same ally squares into enemy traps, so Civilization gets both halves out of ONE token economy plus a statted Construct. deity/Destruction's Charges detonate on the placer's own Free Action from a depth-0 entry, deal energy in a 10 ft radius rather than keen on a 5 ft square, and leave hazards that keep damaging and spreading. heroic/Hunter conceals a trap at depth 0 for no Investiture. leyline/Blue reads intent for free as a depth-0 Passive. What survives as genuinely Fate's is narrower than the profile it wore: an untested Restrain from level 1, the only ally-delegated hazard trigger, and the only narratively-declared delayed trigger — three real clauses, not a tree-wide identity.

crossTreeHooks: Ordained Ground, Bulwark Ground, Weave the Thread, Foreknown Strike and Thread of Inevitability all require an ALLY to voluntarily stand on, or begin its turn on, a specific 5 ft square. Five of nine talents have zero value in a solo scene.

Weave the Thread's granted Reactive Strike scales with the ALLY's weapon and attack bonus, not with your tier. Whether it costs that ally their Reaction is undefined and is a table ruling.

Hexmark adds [Tier] keen 'whenever it takes damage from ANY source' — a pure multiplier on the party's number of damage instances, pairing best with many-small-hits allies and with any tree that applies Afflicted or other ongoing damage ticks (leyline/Red Afterburn, leyline/Black Dark Investiture, deity/Life Adaptive Mutation, heroic/Hunter Deadly Trap).

The tree generates zero Investiture and spends it in seven of nine talents, so it has a hard dependency on Draw Mana. At Tier 1 the treadmill is 1 Action per 1 Investiture, which directly caps the tree's cadence.

Every damage die is sized by GREEN skill rank, Inevitable Snare's DC is your Green, and every placement's Attunement Range is Green-sized — the tree's entire mechanical output is bought with leyline-Green skill investment made outside this tree.

WHITE rank buys the entry gate and nothing else — not even Attunement Range. The tree's only access to healing is White's Draw Mana rider, an attunement key rather than a talent here. One of five toll-booth gates the deity audit names, four of them White.
Snare's damage adds Awareness, an attribute that also sets Investiture maximum — a double dependency on an out-of-tree build choice, and a rare case where the two point the same way.
Thread of Inevitability's declared trigger is usually an event ANOTHER character causes, so the capstone's timing is outsourced to the party and the GM.
Bulwark Ground's advantage denial only has value against enemies that actually generate advantage, and it is the weakest of five corpus effects in that space.

Green's Draw Mana rider creates difficult terrain, which herds enemies into your Snares — a strong seam the tree never mentions and does not mechanically reference, so the synergy is emergent rather than designed.

OVERLAP, not synergy — deity/Civilization: a party already running Civilization gets Ordained Ground's effect twice over from Lay Foundation (same action type, same cost, same +1 all defenses, same tier cap, larger square) and Weave the Thread's shape from Trade Routes (cheaper, and it teleports). Bastion then turns Civilization's ally squares into enemy traps, which is Fate's whole second economy folded into one talent.

OVERLAP — deity/Destruction: Set Charge is Snare with self-detonation at the same entry price; Pinpoint Charge is Inevitable Snare that also ignores deflect and adds Intellect; Cascading Failure and The Unmooring are Thread of Inevitability without the [Tier] throttle. Fate's trap half is Destruction's trap half with the trigger taken away and given to an ally.

topThree: Foreknown Strike — 2 Actions + 2 Investiture once per scene converts the entire trap economy from 'hope the enemy walks in' into a party-detonated bomb, and adds a third [Tier][Die] to every detonation. The single load-bearing talent in the tree, and the only ally-delegated hazard trigger in the corpus — though deity/Destruction gets self-detonation free inside its depth-0 entry, so Fate's best talent is buying a capability another tree treats as table stakes.

Snare — an entry node at level 1 that, for 1 Action + 1 Investiture, delivers [Tier][Die] + Awareness keen AND Restrained for a full round with NO test required, repeatably. Both the tree's damage floor and its best control, and the only untested Restrain in all 365 talents.

Weave the Thread (RESTORED to the top three this pass) — converts an ally's Aid from a 1-focus Reaction into a Free Action, freeing that ally's one Reaction, and adds a Reactive Strike off a trigger the tree itself supplies. Bulwark Ground was promoted into this seat on the strength of being 'the only advantage denial in all 365 talents', and that claim is false (leyline/Green Natural Order also denies advantage; leyline/White Voice of Authority, heroic/Leader Valiant Intervention and heroic/Warrior Defensive Position impose disadvantage, which supersedes it in a tri-state system), so it loses the seat. Two deity capstones at the identical price (Destruction's The Unmooring, Knowledge's The Final Study) buy several times as much.

Bulwark Ground (DEMOTED this pass) — its temp-HP clause is 1 HP per round for the whole of levels 1-5, and its advantage-denial clause is no longer the corpus-unique effect it was credited with: leyline/Green's Natural Order also denies advantage, and three talents in other trees impose disadvantage instead, which is strictly better. What is left is a Passive whose two clauses are both the weakest version of an effect that exists elsewhere, gated on an ally standing on a 5 ft square.

weakTalents.name: Thread of Inevitability
weakTalents.reason: OVERCOSTED. 3 Actions (a whole Slow turn, unplayable on a Fast turn's 2 Actions) + 3 Investiture + once per scene, and the payoff is capped by the tree's own [Tier] sustain limits — at levels 1-5 it detonates exactly ONE Snare and grants exactly ONE free Strike. Its trigger is partly GM-adjudicated. The capstone should have raised the token caps; instead it inherits them. deity/Destruction's The Unmooring and deity/Knowledge's The Final Study both buy far more at the identical price.

weakTalents.name: Bulwark Ground
weakTalents.reason: CORRECTED DOWNWARD this pass. Previously excused as 'half-blank but carried by its second clause'. Both clauses are measurably the weakest version of an effect the corpus already has. The temp-HP clause pays 'equal to your tier' — ONE temporary HP per round for the whole of levels 1-5 — where deity/Civilization's Bonds of Community pays temp HP equal to your WHITE to every ally in any Foundation. The advantage-denial clause is not corpus-unique: leyline/Green's Natural Order denies advantage to every enemy in Attunement Range for the scene, and leyline/White's Voice of Authority, heroic/Leader's Valiant Intervention and heroic/Warrior's Defensive Position IMPOSE disadvantage, which in a tri-state system does everything advantage-denial does and more. Fate's version is also the most constrained of the five (one ally, standing on one 5 ft square).

weakTalents.name: Ordained Ground
weakTalents.reason: Not below the curve in effect, and it DOES deliver the half of the Olvarra fantasy both intent sources assign it. The problem is that it does no design work the corpus had not already done twice: it is deity/Civilization's Lay Foundation (same Free Action, same 1 Investiture, same 'designate a square in Attunement Range... for the scene', same '+1 to all defenses' for allies beginning their turn there, same 'sustain up to your tier') on a 5 ft square instead of 10 ft, and its second clause — Aid at extended range — is deity/Order's Covenant clause, which grants it at full Attunement Range with no square to stand on. A talent that is strictly the smaller version of two existing talents is the least distinctive entry node in the deity atlas.

weakTalents.name: Foreknown Strike / Thread of Inevitability (implementation cannot deliver)
weakTalents.reason: Both say a Snare is triggered 'treating the center of the Snare's space as the triggering character'. A square is not a character; the text names no creature to take the damage or the Restrained condition when the square is empty. Thread of Inevitability adds a second wording flaw: it grants 'a free Strike or Aid against the nearest enemy', but Aid targets an ally. Both are the class of promise an implementation cannot honour without a table ruling. (The earlier entry accusing Weave the Thread of paying twice for Aid remains REMOVED — Ordained Ground changes Aid's RANGE and Weave the Thread changes its ACTION TYPE.)

sustainability.roundsOfGoodOptions: About 2 rounds of unconstrained play, then an indefinite throttled cadence of one placement per round. Opening pool is ~4 Investiture (2 + max(AWA,PRE)) and the tree spends 11 to deploy its full kit once. Round 1 is Ordained Ground (Free, 1 Inv) + Snare (1 Action, 1 Inv) = 2 Inv. At Tier 1 you may hold only ONE unsprung Snare, so a round-2 second Snare is legal only after the first has sprung (otherwise the handler's 'evict: oldest' discards the first); the realistic round 2 is Read the Threads to slide the existing Snare into the revealed path, or a re-place with the Inevitable rider — either way 1-2 Inv, and the pool is empty. From round 3 the character is on the Draw Mana treadmill: at Tier 1 that returns 1 Investiture per Action, so the sustainable loop is Draw Mana (1 Action) + one 1-Investiture placement (1 Action) + 1 spare Action — meaning the Inevitable Snare upgrade is NOT sustainable at levels 1-5. At Tier 2 (L6+) Draw Mana returns 2 per Action, so Draw Mana + Inevitable Snare becomes sustainable indefinitely with an Action to spare. The scene-length purchases (Foreknown Strike, Weave the Thread) are one-time buys that keep paying, so the true profile is 'pay a heavy opening, then run one Snare per round forever'.
sustainability.note: Counted by hand from the nine texts. Only 1 of 9 talents is a Reaction (Hexmark), so this tree suffers almost no contention for the hard 1-Reaction-per-round cap — a genuine structural advantage over leyline/White (7 Reactions competing for one slot, 52% trigger-gated). But 7 of 9 talents wait on someone ELSE acting before they pay out: Snare (an enemy must enter), Inevitable Snare (rider on that), Hexmark (a Snare must fire, then the target must take damage), Bulwark Ground (an ally must begin its turn on the square), Foreknown Strike (an ally must spend a Free Action), Weave the Thread (an ally must be on a square and an enemy must trigger a Snare), Thread of Inevitability (a declared event must occur). Ordained Ground's PLACEMENT resolves on your own turn, but its payout is equally ally-gated, so Read the Threads is the ONLY talent in the tree that both resolves AND pays out under your own control. The deterministic classifier bands deity trees at 0-3 trigger-gated; the text does not support that here and the text wins. The tree is unusually free of Reaction contention while being almost totally dependent on other characters' choices — it never competes with itself, and it never acts alone. The same 7 of 9 talents also spend Investiture the tree cannot replace.
